data.narrative:
Forge Nano is a Series C-stage climate and energy company that has raised $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 private Climate & Energy companies at identical stage (KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy) alongside a broader comp universe of 9 private and 1 public player in the sector.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression uses the $40M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C to next-stage step-ups, yielding $68M. The peer-median approach references the three directly comparable companies, which trade at a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B, implying $1.0B for Forge Nano. This wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity within the climate-tech sector.

The triangulated analysis yields a range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $534M. The gap between stage-progression and peer median reflects uncertainty around capital efficiency and commercialization timeline relative to peers. Key variables affecting resolution include product-market fit validation, pathway to unit economics, and relative technology differentiation versus the comp set. The peer range itself ($700M–$3.0B) underscores valuation sensitivity to execution risk in early-stage climate infrastructure.
